The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a fresh cyber intrusion targeting its National Crime Information Center (NCIC), a nationwide database used by federal, state and local law enforcement agencies to share information on criminal records, warrants and background checks, according to people briefed on the investigation.The latest incident, discovered in recent days, is the second reported breach involving FBI systems in recent months. It comes after a September cyberattack exposed sensitive personal information belonging to nearly every FBI employee and thousands of local law enforcement officials working on bureau task forces.Two people familiar with the latest investigation said apparent hackers had accessed the NCIC database, although the extent of the intrusion and the information potentially compromised remain unclear. The FBI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.The development has raised fresh concerns about the security of systems used by American law enforcement agencies, particularly as the US government faces scrutiny over a series of cyber incidents and technology disruptions affecting critical infrastructure.The latest breach came to light on Thursday, the same day FBI Director Kash Patel appeared on Fox News to discuss the bureau's cybersecurity initiatives.Patel referred to Operation Winter Shield, an initiative aimed at encouraging companies to update their systems and prevent hackers from accessing sensitive information. He also praised the current administration for making changes to protect critical infrastructure.“Other administrations could have made these updates, but they didn’t,” he said. “We are staying ahead of the curve and making up for lost time.”The appearance came amid growing concerns over cybersecurity following high-profile disruptions affecting banks, the National Security Agency and the Federal Aviation Administration's air traffic control system.In September, a hacking group calling itself ShinyHunters claimed to have stolen sensitive information relating to around 38,000 FBI employees through the bureau's jobs portal, FBIJobs.gov.The compromised information reportedly included names, home addresses, mobile phone numbers, FBI email addresses and employee identification numbers. Personal information relating to emergency contacts, including Social Security numbers and personal email addresses, was also exposed.The breach affected nearly every FBI employee, as well as more than 8,000 state and local law enforcement officers who worked on FBI task forces, according to current and former officials cited in a separate report by MS NOW.An internal FBI message said the exposed records contained sensitive personal information. The hackers released a sample of 5,000 records but later said they did not intend to publish the entire database.The FBI confirmed that the incident involved a failure of a platform managed by a third-party vendor.“The FBI continues to investigate the recent Cyber incident, which we have confirmed involved a failure of a platform managed by a third-party vendor,” an FBI spokesman said in a statement.An FBI cybersecurity agent attributed the breach to failures in the bureau's security arrangements.“This was a vulnerability that supposedly they thought they patched, but managed to miss one of the ways to patch it,” the agent said in a text message, adding that the cause was “definitely incompetence.”The agent also questioned why such sensitive information had been accessible through an internet-facing system.The sensitive employee information that was stolen “should never have been tied to the Internet, either. It belonged on our internal system and some dumbass moved it all” to an internet-facing system, the agent said.The agent added that the FBI had obtained chats in which the hackers expressed disbelief at how easily they could access the information.Cybersecurity experts said ShinyHunters exploited a vulnerability in Oracle PeopleSoft, a human resources software platform used by the FBI.Google's threat intelligence experts had issued a public warning in June about the vulnerability, after which the FBI took steps to strengthen its systems, according to two cybersecurity experts familiar with the matter.However, the hackers reportedly found a way around the FBI's security patch.An FBI official told MS NOW that the breach resulted from a vulnerability in software maintained by a third-party vendor. The official did not respond to allegations of negligence within the bureau.The hackers did not penetrate the FBI's core investigative network or classified systems, according to current and former officials. However, the stolen information could still pose a serious security risk.Experts have warned that foreign adversaries, including China and Russia, could use the information to identify FBI personnel working on sensitive investigations, potentially creating opportunities for blackmail or recruitment.“Beyond causing significant reputational damage to the FBI, the incident poses a longer-term national security threat to the United States,” researchers from the Center for Strategic and International Studies said in an analysis released this week.The breach has also drawn comparisons with the 2015 cyberattack on the US Office of Personnel Management, attributed to Chinese intelligence agents. That incident exposed sensitive information relating to millions of federal employees, including fingerprints and details from security clearance applications.The September breach was also described as a possible retaliation attack after the FBI issued a public advisory about ShinyHunters in May.The hacking group reportedly demanded that the bureau withdraw or correct the advisory, which described the group as threat actors known for stealing personal and corporate information.In a message posted on the dark web, ShinyHunters said it had not targeted the FBI for money and gave the agency a week to address what it considered false allegations, threatening to release the full databases otherwise.The FBI had said it was investigating whether the hackers had accessed its own systems or those of a third-party provider.The group, believed to have originated in France, has been linked to several high-profile cyberattacks targeting technology companies, financial institutions and other organisations.The FBI has also faced earlier security breaches. In 2023, hackers accessed a computer system used by the bureau's New York field office for investigations into child sexual exploitation. The system reportedly included images related to the investigation involving Jeffrey Epstein.The latest intrusion into the NCIC database adds to the growing list of cybersecurity challenges facing the bureau. The investigation is expected to establish the extent of the access, the information potentially compromised and whether the incident is connected to earlier attacks.
Article Summary: Second reported breach involving FBI systems in recent months. In September, hackers claimed to have stolen sensitive information relating to around 38,000 FBI employees through the bureau's jobs portal, FBIJobs.gov. The FBI confirmed that the incident involved a failure of a platform managed by a third-party vendor.

Article Title: 'Get married, have more babies': Karoline Leavitt to Americans as Pew predicts Muslims to outnumber Christians by 2035
Article Text:
Ex-White House Press Secy's advice as Muslims projected to outnumber Christians

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt has urged Christians to marry, have more children and raise them in the church after projections by the Pew Research Center suggested that Muslims could overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group by 2035.Sharing a screenshot of a Washington Post report on Friday, Leavitt, now a Fox News contributor, wrote on X,: “Get married, have more babies, raise them in the church, and teach them to love America.”The article, titled “Muslims to outnumber Christians worldwide by 2035, study finds”, attributed the projections to the Pew Research Center and Poland's Center for Advanced Studies of Population and Religion (CASPAR).The projections, released by Pew on Thursday, estimate that the global Muslim population will reach 2.57 billion by 2035, compared with 2.52 billion Christians. In 2020, Christians numbered an estimated 2.27 billion worldwide, while Muslims accounted for 2.02 billion, according to the research centre.Pew said both religions are expected to grow, but the Muslim population is projected to increase at a faster rate.The difference is largely attributed to fertility rates, with Muslim women having more children on average than women belonging to other major religious groups.“It's the babies,” Pew senior demographer Conrad Hackett said, explaining that births and deaths play a much greater role in the projected population changes than religious conversion.According to Pew estimates, the total fertility rate for Muslim women was 3.1 children per woman during 2020-2025. The corresponding figure for Christian women was 2.5, while the average for women belonging to other religious groups was 1.6. A fertility rate of around 2.1 children per woman is generally considered necessary for a generation to replace itself.Leavitt left her role as the press secretary at the end of August, after serving in the post since January 2025. Announcing her decision in August, she said she had found it difficult to balance the demands of the job with motherhood after returning from maternity leave following the birth of her second child in May. She described her departure as a “bittersweet decision” and said she would continue to support US president Donald Trump as an outside adviser. She joined Fox News as a contributor in November.The research also highlights that Muslim population growth is not necessarily taking place at the expense of Christians. Pew projects that both groups will increase in numbers over the coming decades, with their growth driven primarily by natural population change rather than people switching faiths.Between 2020 and 2070, Muslims are projected to gain 1.6 billion people through natural population change, compared with an increase of 792 million among Christians. Religious switching is expected to have a smaller impact, with Pew projecting a net loss of 105 million Christians and eight million Muslims over the period.Looking further ahead, Pew estimates that the global Muslim population could exceed 3.6 billion by 2070, while the Christian population would remain just below three billion.
Article Summary: Ex-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt urges Christians to marry, have more children and raise them in the church. Pew Research Center projections suggest Muslims could overtake Christians as the world's largest religious group by 2035. In 2020, Christians numbered an estimated 2.27 billion worldwide, while Muslims accounted for 2.02 billion.

Article Title: 'Grow a spine': Youth Congress workers storm Meta office premises in Hyderabad; issue ultimatum
Article Text:
Telangana Youth Congress leaders organized a protest at Meta's office in Raidurgam over blocked accounts of their leaders

'Grow a spine'





HYDERABAD: Telangana Youth Congress leaders staged a protest and allegedly vandalised property at Meta’s office in Raidurgam on Friday, accusing the company of blocking the social media accounts of national-level Youth Congress leaders Uday Bhanu and Manish Sharma Police said around 25 Congress activists carrying placards entered the access-controlled Sky View premises, which houses Meta’s office, around 3pm.The protesters raised slogans, ran through the property and damaged flower pots and other objects in a corridor before staging a sit-in.The protesters accused Meta of working under BJP’s influence and demanded restoration of the blocked accounts.Raidurgam police reached the premises and attempted to control the protesters, who allegedly created panic and tried to evade them. Police initially said 20 protesters were taken into custody.Raidurgam inspector T Bhupathi later said Telangana Youth Congress state president Jakkidi Shiva Charan Reddy and 20 others were taken into preventive custody when they arrived to protest against Meta’s office.All were released on bail after providing the necessary sureties.Later in the day the Indian Youth Congress (IYC) escalated its confrontation with social media giant, issuing a sharp seven-day ultimatum accusing the platform of political censorship and acting at the behest of the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).In a post on X addressing "BJP ka Beta - META," the Youth Congress declared that India is a democracy rather than "Modi's private property," and warned the company to restore restricted accounts and posts within seven days.Calling on Meta to "grow a spine" and operate as a neutral platform rather than a "BJP's frontal organisation," and threatened escalations "in the courts, on the streets, and at your offices too" if its demands are not met.
Article Summary: Telangana Youth Congress leaders staged a protest and allegedly vandalised property at Meta’s office in Raidurgam on Friday. Police said around 25 Congress activists carrying placards entered the access-controlled Sky View premises, which houses Meta's office, around 3pm. The protesters accused Meta of working under BJP's influence and demanded restoration of the blocked accounts.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu horror: Woman raped, murdered inside train coach
Article Text:
50-year-old woman was found murdered in a train coach at Nagercoil Junction railway station.





MADURAI: A woman was allegedly raped and beaten to death inside a stationary train coach at Nagercoil Junction railway station, which was subsequently parked at the railway yard for repairs. Railway police on Friday arrested a 31-year-old man, identified as Ayyappan , in connection with the crime, which went undetected for four days.The decomposed body of the unidentified woman, aged around 50, was discovered around 8am on Nov 18 beneath a seat in the rear coach reserved for persons with disabilities on train No. 16366, stationed at Yard No. 13. Based on a complaint from Nagercoil East village administrative officer, THE railway police registered a case of unnatural death. Following an autopsy that established murder, the case was altered to include the charge.A special team headed by railway police inspector Catherine Sujatha examined CCTV camera footage from the station and spotted a man wearing a white shirt and dhoti getting down from the coach at 8am on Nov 14, when it was stationed near Platforms 4 and 5.“Further investigation traced the crime to around 12.30am that day, nearly seven-and-a-half hours before the suspect was seen leaving the coach,” said a senior police officer.According to an official release, the woman was walking near Platform 5 around 12.30am when the accused spotted her. He allegedly grabbed her hand, forcibly dragged her into the unoccupied coach reserved for persons with disabilities and raped her. He then repeatedly punched her, kicked and stamped on different parts of her body. Police said she died from severe injuries sustained in the assault.The accused, Ayyappan, son of Johnson, hails from Chenbagaramanputhoor in Kanyakumari district. Police said he had been roaming around for the past four months. Following his arrest and interrogation, he was produced before a court and remanded in judicial custody.Meanwhile, police are continuing efforts to establish the identity of the murdered woman and trace her family. The incident has raised serious questions about security at railway stations, particularly how such a crime occurred inside a stationary coach and the body remained undiscovered for four days.
Article Summary: The decomposed body of the unidentified woman, aged around 50, was discovered around 8am on Nov 18 beneath a seat in the rear coach reserved for persons with disabilities on train No. 16366, stationed at Yard No. 13. Railway police on Friday arrested a 31-year-old man, identified as Ayyappan, in connection with the crime, which went undetected for four days.

Article Title: Man kills wife in Bengaluru over suspected affair; skeleton found in bag two months later
Article Text:
Deceased Sujatha and Accused Fayaz Pasha





BENGALURU: A marital dispute allegedly fuelled by the husband’s suspicions about his wife’s relationship with another man ended in murder. A 25-year-old man killed his 34-year-old wife and concealed her body under garbage in Gundanjaneya Temple Park in Kodigehalli, police investigations revealed. The crime came to light over two months later when the woman’s skeletal remains were found.Police have identified the deceased as Sujatha and arrested her second husband, Fayaz Pasha alias Kalu, a native of Chikkaballapur. The skeletal remains were found in a gunny bag on Nov 6. Kodigehalli police found an Aadhaar card and PAN card in a pouch among the skeletal remains, while her skull was found 30 metres away from the bag.Based on the preliminary investigation, police said Sujatha’s first husband had died about five years ago. Sujatha, who lived at Jakkur Layout, left her five children at her sister’s home and started working as a ragpicker.She later became close to Pasha, who was nine years younger. He was also a ragpicker and construction labourer. The two got married around five months ago.However, their relationship soon turned sour, with Pasha suspecting that Sujatha’s conduct was not appropriate. He left her following differences over the issue.Later, Sujatha approached him and persuaded him to return, expressing her desire to resume their life together. However, after Pasha returned, the couple started quarrelling again. They lived in parks, bus stands and other places.During one such dispute, Pasha slit her throat in the park and killed her, police said. He then packed her body in a gunny bag used to collect rags, concealed it under garbage dumped in one of the corners of the park and escaped.Based on her Aadhaar and PAN cards, police learnt about her marriage to Pasha. They traced him at Raitara Santhe in Yelahanka and nabbed him on Nov 18. He has been taken into police custody for investigation.A senior officer said Pasha confessed that they fought after getting drunk in the park at night over two months ago, and he slit her throat with a knife.The skull was pulled out by a dog in early Nov, and walkers noticed it and alerted police.
Article Summary: Police have identified the deceased as Sujatha and arrested her second husband, Fayaz Pasha alias Kalu, a native of Chikkaballapur. The skeletal remains were found in a gunny bag on Nov 6. The skull was pulled out by a dog in early Nov, and walkers noticed it and alerted police.

Article Title: Madhya Pradesh horror: Man held for strangling wife after phone dispute in Balaghat
Article Text:
In Balaghat district, a woman named Sushma Raut was murdered by her husband Dinesh Raut (AI image)





BHOPAL: A quarrel over late-night mobile phone use ended in the murder of a woman in Balaghat district, with her husband accused of strangling her at their home in Siwangaht village.The victim, identified as Sushma Raut, had been married to Dinesh Raut for three years. According to police, she was using her mobile phone late on Thursday night, disturbing her husband’s sleep.Police said Dinesh then allegedly assaulted her and strangled her. When Sushma showed no signs of movement for around 10 to 15 minutes, he panicked and called family members, claiming that her health had suddenly deteriorated.He subsequently took her to a hospital, where doctors declared her dead.An argument broke out, during which Dinesh allegedly slapped her. Sushma retaliated with a slap, escalating the dispute.The suspicious circumstances surrounding Sushma’s death led police to question Dinesh. During interrogation, he allegedly confessed to killing his wife. Police said he was also known to consume alcohol, and the couple frequently quarrelled.
Article Summary: Sushma Raut was killed by her husband Dinesh Raut in Balaghat district. Police say she was using her mobile phone late on Thursday night, disturbing her husband’s sleep. An argument broke out, during which he allegedly slapped her. Sushma retaliated with a slap, escalating the dispute.

Article Title: Adani power project in Satara: ‘Nod covers 4 villages, excavation on at 5th’
Article Text:
Adani Green Energy Ltd's Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar.





MUMBAI: Amid a row over work on Adani Green Energy Ltd’s (AGEL) 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project beginning in Satara’s Patan taluka despite lack of approval from National Board for Wildlife (NBWL), the state forest department’s honorary wildlife warden for the district has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board (MPCB) alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway in Sawarghar village, which was not listed on the environmental clearance (EC) granted by the Union forest ministry on Feb 11 last year.The honorary wildlife warden, Rohan Bhate, said the EC specified only four villages that stand to be affected—Nivade, Tondoshi, Kalambe and Jalu—in the district.A spokesperson from Adani Group said the EC covers the four villages as well as Dafalwadi, and the company later purchased private land in Sawarghar to set up temporary accommodation for workers. The company said such an accommodation was included in the project layout approval from Central Electricity Authority. It said the project has all the relevant clearances and initial works are in progress at the site.The Tarali project, estimated at Rs 5,675 crore, is planned over 150.7 hectares of private land.In his letter to MPCB member-secretary Rahul Rekhawar, Bhate claimed that the activity in Sawarghar did not have the required EC and NBWL’s approval, and sought urgent intervention and an independent investigation.Rekhawar confirmed that MPCB has received Bhate’s letter and said it is investigating the allegations.Amol Satpute, MPCB sub-regional officer in Satara, said a team from the pollution regulator inspected the Sawarghar site on Friday, where excavation was underway. Satpute said when officials questioned the site supervisor, they were told the developer was levelling land to set up a labour camp for the Tarali project. He said a report would be submitted to higher authorities.Bhate said the situation raised questions about the geographical scope and validity of the EC in relation to the work being carried out at Sawarghar. He questioned whether MPCB had verified that the proponent had obtained environmental and wildlife clearances for all land parcels involved before issuing the mandatory ‘consent to establish’ (CTE) that allows construction to begin. He said MPCB cannot distance itself from responsibility because the CTE stage is a crucial regulatory checkpoint.Bhate requested an immediate site inspection and preparation of an official panchnama by MPCB officials to document the extent of excavation and construction, the machinery deployed, and the exact location of the work. He said if any excavation or construction is found to have started without statutory approvals, authorities should register the appropriate offence and initiate legal proceedings against responsible individuals and project authorities.He also asked MPCB to determine whether activity at Sawarghar is covered by the Feb 11, 2025, EC and whether all applicable environmental permissions for that specific location have been obtained. In addition, he sought verification of whether prior approval from the NBWL’s standing committee was secured wherever legally required.Bhate said the proposed project falls within the deemed eco-sensitive zone of Koyna wildlife sanctuary and the Sahyadri tiger reserve, making strict scrutiny under environmental and wildlife protection provisions essential. He requested that the matter be assigned to an impartial higher-level authority for an independent inquiry rather than being examined only by officials linked to project clearances. Pending verification, he asked for directions to prevent any further unauthorised excavation or construction at the site.Sources said AGEL has not yet complied with the stop-work order issued on Nov 13 by Satpute, in his capacity as the Satara division’s deputy conservator of forests, for starting work on the project without NBWL’s approval. Adani Group had earlier said the proposal had been submitted to NBWL. Satpute said he would need to check whether the developer had followed the order.
Article Summary: Adani Green Energy Ltd’s 1,500MW Tarali pumped storage project is under investigation due to alleged unauthorized work at Sawarghar. Forest department's honorary wildlife warden has written to Maharashtra Pollution Control Board alleging that large-scale excavation and construction is underway.

Article Title: Buffs break away from fight, charge at 8-year-old boy, trample him to death in Ujjain
Article Text:
Eight-year-old boy named Yuvraj was killed by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain.





UJJAIN: In a tragic turn of events, an eight-year-old boy was trampled to death by charging buffaloes while watching a buffalo fight with his father on Friday. The incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s Ujjain district.The buffalo fight, it turns out, is a traditional event held on the occasion of Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi, a calendar festival.The bout between two buffaloes was being staged in a field near the govt school. Around 2 pm, Akash arrived with his son Yuvraj to catch the fight. He stood at the edge of the crowd, while the boy sat close to him, eating poha (a popular local snack).As the buffaloes, released from their pen or enclosure, charged towards the spectators, one climbed onto Yuvraj’s chest. His father jumped to his rescue, and was joined by some bystanders who eventually helped pull the child out from under the marauding feet of the buffs.The boy was rushed to a hospital where the doctors declared him dead on arrival.Akash, a taxi driver, said Yuvraj, a Class 3 student, was his only son. “The buffaloes were in a fight and had locked horns. My son was sitting close to me as we watched the fight. However, all of a sudden, the buffaloes came charging in our direction and trampled my child,” the father said, laying the blame on the organiser.A private hospital in Chandesari declared him dead on arrival, after which his body was taken to the district hospital at Charak Bhawan, where a post-mortem was conducted before the last remains were handed to the family.Nagjhiri station in-charge Rakesh Bharti said such events are illegal, adding that the incident was being investigated. He said the organiser had been warned two days earlier and had promised not to hold the event, yet went ahead with it.A case of unnatural death was registered, the officer said, adding that a criminal case will be filed against the accused once the inquiry establishes the facts. Statements from the family are yet to be recorded.Local residents said a similar event three to four years ago had led to stone pelting at the police.
Article Summary: Eight-year-old trampled to death by charging buffaloes during a traditional fight in Ujjain. Incident took place at Hamukhedi on Dewas Road, in the Nagjhiri police station area of Madhya Pradesh’s UJJain district.

Article Title: Rajasthan couple murdered by relative over vacating rented room
Article Text:
Couple killed by a distant relative following their request for him to leave his rental space





RAJKOT: A couple were killed and two of their relatives seriously injured when a distant relative of theirs attacked them with a nail-studded wooden club, as he held a grudge about being given notice to vacate the room they had rented to him, in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday.According to the FIR registered at Atkot police station on Friday, the deceased are Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35). The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodakiya (35), Prakash’s sister-in-law, and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew.Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Ghodakiya, a resident of the same village, on charges of murder.Talking to TOI, Jasdan assistant superintendent of police Naveen Chakravarthy Repudi said the accused was unemployed and had been given a room to stay by the victims. “When they asked him to vacate the room, he held a grudge about it. He later attacked them with a club which had nails in it, which caused grievous head injuries to the victims,” he said.According to Labhu’s complaint, around 3.30pm on Thursday, she had gone to Prakash’s house to bring back her young son, Vraj, There was a knock on the door and when. Vilas opened it they and saw Ashok — a distant cousin of Prakash’s — carrying a wooden club.He began hurling abuses.When Labhu and Vilas objected to his language, Ashok allegedly threatened to kill them and swung the club at Labhu’s head. She suffered an injury to her left palm while trying to block the first blow, before a second strike hit the left side of her head.When Vilas intervened to save Labhu, Ashok struck her repeatedly on the head with the club. Hearing their screams, Prakash rushed out, followed by Puri, who was sitting at a kirana shop behind the house. Both were allegedly hit on their heads until they collapsed.The accused fled after Labhu’s eldest brother-in-law, Ramesh, arrived. The two injured victims are getting treatment at a hospital.
Article Summary: Vilas Ghodakiya (32) and her husband, Prakash (35), were killed in Jangvad village of Jasdan taluka on Thursday. The injured include the complainant, Labhu Ghodkiya (35) and Puri, the wife of Labhu’s nephew. Atkot police arrested the accused, Ashok Godakiya, on charges of murder.

Article Title: Bihar horror: Student dragged, molested; male friend assaulted, 3 arrested after video surfaces
Article Text:
Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student





PATNA: Police arrested three men within 12 hours of an incident in which a student was allegedly molested, assaulted and verbally abused in the Bochahan police station area of Muzaffarpur district.A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused.The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, son of Shivnath Sharma and a resident of Ward No. 1 in Kashirampur village; Vishal Kumar, son of Ram Kumar Sharma; and Ujjwal Kumar, son of Lal Babu Rai, a resident of Bhorhan village. All three were taken to Bochahan police station for questioning before being formally booked in the case.Alay Vats, Sub-Divisional Police Officer (East-I), said the incident came to light on November 19 after the video surfaced on social media."In the video, the accused molested the girl and indulged in indecent behaviour, while her friend was assaulted. Taking the matter seriously, officers began verifying the footage, examined the circumstances of the incident and identified those involved. Following the investigation and verification of the location, a police team conducted raids and apprehended all three accused within 12 hours," he said.Police also seized two mobile phones allegedly used to record and circulate the video. An FIR was registered under relevant sections of the law, and the process of sending the arrested men to judicial custody was initiated.Bochahan SHO Yashwant Kumar Mishra said police acted immediately after receiving information about the incident and intensified efforts to identify and arrest the accused. He confirmed that three men had been arrested, two mobile phones seized and further investigation was under way.The arrests were made by a team from Bochahan police station under the supervision of SDPO East-I, with the SHO leading the operation.
Article Summary: Muzaffarpur district witnessed a rapid police response as three men were arrested within 12 hours for the alleged molestation of a student. A video of the incident reportedly circulated on social media, prompting police to launch an investigation and identify the accused. The arrested men were identified as Anurag Kumar, Vishal Kumar and Ujjwal Kumar.

Article Title: After Mumbai unit's Rs 1 lakh offer, Pimpri Chinchwad Shiv Sena (UBT) announces cash reward for slapping Shaina NC
Article Text:
Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions

Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph

Poll Vote & Share your view How should political disputes like this be addressed? Through peaceful dialogue Through legal action Through public protests 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





PIMPRI CHINCHWAD: Shiv Sena (UBT) has announced a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps Shiv Sena leader Shaina NC, escalating the political row over an incident involving a photograph of party founder Balasaheb Thackeray.Making the announcement on Thursday, Shiv Sena (UBT)'s Pimpri Chinchwad unit president Chetan Pawar told reporters that the reward was being offered in response to a similar announcement by a Shiv Sena (UBT) office-bearer from Mumbai."As everyone knows, our party office-bearer from Mumbai has already announced a reward of Rs 1 lakh for anyone who slaps Shaina NC. Similarly, we, as the Pimpri Chinchwad unit of Shiv Sena (UBT), announce a reward of Rs 71,000 for anyone who slaps her," Pawar said.The controversy erupted on Wednesday during a press conference organised by the Shinde-led Shiv Sena in Mumbai to protest against references to Hindutva ideologue V D Savarkar in Congress leader Sonia Gandhi's memoir, Belonging: A Journey of Love.During the protest, party leaders tore pages from the book. Shaina was also seen tearing a portion of a photograph depicting Balasaheb Thackeray striking an effigy of Congress leader Mani Shankar Aiyar with a slipper.The incident was captured on camera and drew criticism from Shiv Sena (UBT) leaders.Shaina denied deliberately disrespecting Balasaheb, maintaining that she had torn the portion showing Aiyar and not the photograph of the late Shiv Sena founder. Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also defended her explanation.On Thursday, Shaina apologised to Balasaheb's admirers if her actions had hurt their sentiments, while insisting that she had no intention of disrespecting him.The incident has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde.
Article Summary: Shiv Sena (UBT) has offered a reward in response to similar announcements made by rival factions. Row over Balasaheb Thackeray's photograph has triggered a fresh confrontation between the rival Shiv Sena factions led by Uddhav Thackersay and Eknath Shinde.

Article Title: Brent crude falls over $1 as Trump signals fresh US strikes on Iran are unlikely
Article Text:
Crude oil eases after Trump's remarks

Trump warns Iran despite ruling out fresh strikes

Hormuz caught in chokehold

Oil prices opened lower on Monday, with Brent crude briefly shedding more than $1 a barrel.The dip comes after US President Donald Trump said that fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, or 0.17%, to $90.68 a barrel.Trump's comments offered an indication that the US could avoid another round of military action against Iran, provided Tehran agreed to what he described as a strong deal. However, reports from both countries of shipping being hit in and around the Strait of Hormuz kept concerns over disruptions to the strategic waterway alive."It depends on whether or not they sign a very strong agreement," Trump told CNN in a phone interview. "The answer is, highly unlikely it's going to be necessary."In a 20-minute telephone interview with CNN, Trump repeated five times that renewed military intervention was unlikely if Iran made tangible progress in negotiations over its nuclear programme and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.The US president, however, warned that Washington had identified 38 Iranian bridges that could be destroyed within an hour if further military action became necessary."We have 38 bridges in our site that we can knock down in literally one hour. They’ll all be down," Trump told CNN.The remarks come amid continued disruption to crude oil supplies through the Strait of Hormuz, which has now lasted for over eight months. The disruption has affected refinery operations across major Asian and Middle Eastern economies.According to the US Energy Information Administration (EIA), global refinery activity fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 after the Middle East conflict broke out.Data from energy intelligence firm Kpler showed that global refinery inputs dropped by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d), or 6%, in April-June compared with the previous quarter. However, they recovered by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter as refiners adapted to changing trade flows and alternative supply routes.Countries that rely heavily on crude supplies passing through the Strait of Hormuz were among the worst affected.China saw the biggest decline, with refinery inputs falling by 2.1 million b/d in the second quarter and a further 0.8 million b/d in the third quarter.India, South Korea and Japan together recorded a drop of more than 1 million b/d in crude oil inputs in the second quarter. Their combined inputs recovered by 0.8 million b/d in the following quarter.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures fell 52 cents, or 0.53%, to $97.80 a barrel. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude futures slipped 15 cents, to $90.68 a barrels. US President Donald Trump said fresh American strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” if negotiations between the two countries made progress.

NEW DELHI: Former Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID), taking a step towards her planned return from India in December.The information comes from a Monday letter sent by Hasina’s lawyers to the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's embassy in Delhi, Preeti Rahman, Reuters reported.Hasina's lawyers at London-based Matrix Chambers requested the issuance of fresh documents. They cited the reported cancellation of her existing passport and NID by Bangladesh's interim government and other authorities."In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote.The letter urged the authorities to process the applications "expeditiously", citing Hasina's Bangladeshi nationality and the country's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".However, Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"."She is a fugitive criminal. We have an active extradition treaty with India. We want her handed over," Bangladesh state minister for foreign affairs, Humaiun Kobir, told reporters."Should we treat her like an ordinary commercial traveller and tell her ​to come and visit her ​in-laws’ residence?" Kobir jibed.According to Reuters, the request is the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. Her return could reignite political and legal tensions as Bangladesh attempts to restore stability and her Awami League party remains banned.Hasina intends to return and surrender before a court. Her aides said on Monday that the date would be announced after the completion of various formalities.Last week, the exiled leader the Associated Press she would prefer dying in her own land, among her own people.“If death is my destiny, I would rather die on the soil of my own country, among my own people,” Hasina said.In November 2025, Bangladesh's war-crimes tribunal sentenced Hasina to death in absentia for ordering a crackdown on the student-led uprising. She has denied the charges, rejected the verdict and questioned the legitimacy of the trial.The crackdown killed hundreds of protesters and left thousands injured. According to United Nations data cited by the Associated Press, nearly 1,400 people were killed during the unrest.Bangladesh has repeatedly sought Hasina's extradition from India. New Delhi has said the request is being examined through legal channels.Hasina's Awami League was Bangladesh's largest political party before it was banned following her removal from office. Several of its leaders and members have since been jailed, while others have gone into self-imposed exile in India and elsewhere.Having served as Prime Minister for 20 years across multiple terms, Hasina retains support among sections of the population. Her return could deepen political divisions as the country continues to deal with the aftermath of the upheaval.It could also have implications for Bangladesh's strained relationship with India, which deteriorated sharply after New Delhi gave the former prime minister refuge.
Article Summary: Sheikh Hasina has formally sought a new passport and national identity card (NID) The request is reportedly the clearest indication yet that Hasina is taking steps to act on her stated intention to return in December. Bangladesh denied Hasina’s request, stating that the country does not provide "passport to a terrorist"

Article Title: US next aircraft carrier to honour Pearl Harbor hero, Navy rejects name change to Trump
Article Text:
A portrait of Doris Miller showing a Navy Cross received in a ceremony at Pearl Harbor (US National Archives and Records Administration

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Donald Trump may be getting a battleship named after him, but he will not get his name on America's next aircraft carrier.The US Navy has ruled out renaming its next Ford-class carrier after the president, confirming that the warship will retain the name USS Doris Miller, honouring the Black American sailor who became a hero during Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor in 1941.The confirmation comes after months of speculation over a possible name change, with reports in August suggesting that navy officials had discussed renaming the carrier after Trump. The proposal would have replaced the name of Doris Miller, whose bravery during the December 7, 1941, attack on Pearl Harbor made him one of the most celebrated figures in US naval history.The Navy has now put those reports to rest. A spokesperson for acting navy secretary Hung Cao told CNN, "There is no intention to change the name of the USS Doris Miller."The statement effectively rules out the reported proposal and confirms that the next Ford-class aircraft carrier will continue to carry the name of the World War II hero.But why was the carrier's name being reconsidered in the first place? According to CNN's August report, navy officials had held internal discussions about renaming the vessel after Trump. The discussions reportedly came amid a broader push to revisit the navy's ship-naming guidelines, with some officials favouring names of US presidents and senior military leaders for aircraft carriers.The proposal, however, would have meant dropping the name of a sailor whose actions during one of the most defining moments in American military history earned him national recognition.Doris 'Dorie' Miller was serving aboard the USS West Virginia when Japanese forces launched their surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941. Despite having no formal training in operating anti-aircraft guns, Miller took control of one and fired at Japanese aircraft while helping evacuate wounded sailors, including his commanding officer.Miller's bravery earned him the Navy Cross in 1942, making him the first African American sailor to receive the decoration. His recognition was particularly significant at a time when the US navy maintained racial segregation and Black sailors were largely assigned to service roles rather than combat positions.Miller was later killed in November 1943 when a Japanese submarine torpedoed the aircraft carrier USS Liscome Bay during the Battle of Makin.The Navy's decision comes as Trump is already pursuing plans for a new class of warships bearing his name.In December 2025, the president announced the proposed Trump-class battleships as part of his 'Golden Fleet' initiative, with the first vessel expected to be named USS Defiant.The plan would make Trump the namesake of an entirely new class of US navy warships, even as the Navy has ruled out putting his name on the next Ford-class aircraft carrier.
Article Summary: The US Navy has ruled out renaming its next Ford-class carrier after the president. The warship will retain the name USS Doris Miller, honouring the Black American sailor who became a hero during Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor. The confirmation comes after months of speculation over a possible name change.

Article Title: Bangladesh wage protests: Clashes erupt between garment workers and police, dozens of factories shut
Article Text:

Tensions escalated in Bangladesh's Ashulia on Saturday as garment workers demanding a hike in minimum wages clashed with security forces. Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control, The Daily Star reported.According to the news agency ANI, the confrontation took place around 11 am in the Kathgara area along the Zirabo-Bismail road. Workers from several garment factories had stopped production and joined the protest, according to the report.Eyewitnesses told The daily star that workers at multiple factories in Kathgara first entered their workplaces before stopping work. They later organised a rally and attempted to block the road around 10:45 am after factory management announced holidays.Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan, superintendent of police at industrial police-1 in Ashulia, said in a text message around noon that the situation had returned to normal."Some unruly workers were trying to create instability at the garment factories that remained operational in the Kathgara area. Industrial police and other forces intervened to keep the situation under control," Bhuiyan said.Earlier on Saturday, at least 50 factories in the Savar-Ashulia industrial belt announced holidays following work stoppages.However, most factories in the area had started operations as usual in the morning, industrial police told the newspaper.The latest clashes come amid continuing protests by garment workers across Bangladesh over demands for higher wages and better working conditions.On Tuesday, garment workers staged demonstrations in Mirpur, Dhaka, demanding that the minimum monthly wage be increased to 30,000 taka. The protests came as labour unrest spread across the country's textile industry, forcing several factories to suspend operations.Protesters also attempted to block roads but were stopped by police, who intervened to prevent traffic disruptions and maintain law and order.Garment workers in several parts of Bangladesh have been staging strikes to demand better pay, with demonstrations leading to factory closures in multiple industrial areas, DW reported.Separately, a group of workers gathered at Padmar Mor in the Hemayetpur area of Savar around 3 pm on Monday, briefly disrupting the area. Police asked them to disperse peacefully, following which they cleared the road without further incident, Dhaka Tribune reported.Meanwhile, around 40 factories remained closed in the Savar and Ashulia industrial zones on Monday, according to industrial police.Of these, 27 factories were shut under section 13(1) of the Bangladesh labour act, while nine were declared closed indefinitely. The remaining factories observed general holidays.Bhuiyan said workers at one factory refused to resume work after the lunch break and continued sitting inside the premises, prompting management to declare a holiday. Employees at two other factories also stopped work and staged sit-in protests inside their workplaces.However, workers at other factories across the industrial areas continued their operations peacefully, he added.
Article Summary: Police fired tear gas to disperse the protesters and bring the situation under control. The confrontation took place around 11 am in the Kathgara area along the Zirabo-Bismail road. Workers from several garment factories had stopped production and joined the protest.

Article Title: D-Company shooter killed by cops, days after gang war murder in Delhi
Article Text:
Naseem Durrani, an operative linked to Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company, met his end in a police encounter. He was the main suspect in the murder of Sameer, who was attacked violently

20-25 rounds fired

Asked to surrender, Durrani opened fire at cops





NEW DELHI: Days after a brazen daylight murder near Delhi law minister Kapil Mishra's camp office in northeast Delhi, gangster Naseem Durrani, the prime accused in the case and a key operative of Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company, was shot dead Friday morning in an encounter with a joint team of Delhi Police Crime Branch and Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force in Bulandshahr following a dramatic chase.Durrani was wanted in connection with the Nov 16 murder of Sameer, who was shot around 20 times in an attack suspected to have stemmed from an ongoing gang rivalry and a struggle for supremacy in northeast Delhi. Sameer worked at a manufacturing unit and was suspected to be part of a rival gang, as per police sources.Durrani was tracked during the early hours near Sikandra bypass. CCTV footage from the area showed him riding a scooter and repeatedly looking back at the pursuing police personnel. Cops said during the chase, his scooter skidded, causing him to fall. Armed with two .32-bore pistols, he allegedly opened fire at the police team, triggering an exchange of gunfire.Special commissioner of police (Crime) HGS Dhaliwal said a joint team of Delhi Police Crime Branch and UP STF intercepted Durrani, who carried a Rs 50,000 reward, during the intervening night of Nov 19 and 20 near Jat Chowk, under Sikandrabad police station limits in Bulandshahr district.When challenged and asked to surrender, Durrani allegedly pulled out a pistol and opened indiscriminate fire at the police personnel. The team retaliated in selfdefence, leading to an intense exchange of fire in which 20-25 rounds were fired. DCP (crime) Sanjeev Yadav said Durrani sustained bullet injuries during the exchange and was rushed to the nearest hospital, where doctors declared him brought dead.The crime branch team involved in the operation comprised ACP Vivekanand Pathak and inspectors Man Singh and Sunder Gautam. As per police records, Durrani was wanted in two other criminal cases.In one case registered at Khajuri Khas police station on May 26 under murder and Arms Act provisions, he was identified as the main shooter in the killing of Raja Mewati. The victim was found injured following a firing incident at F Block, Khajuri Khas, and was later declared brought dead at hospital.In another case registered at Loni police station in Ghaziabad, a violent altercation took place over a monetary dispute on the night of June 11 on Eidgah Road, near Tyagi Market.A man named Shahbaz allegedly owed Rs 25,000 to Durrani for the purchase of a motorcycle and had been called by the latter to settle the outstanding amount.Accompanied by Saleem, Shahbaz offered to pay only Rs 12,000, which Durrani rejected. The disagreement escalated into an exchange of abuses, followed by a physical fight. When a female passerby intervened and asked the men to stop, Shahbaz and Saleem allegedly opened fire at her with the intention to kill.During the subsequent investigation and interrogation, Durrani’s name also surfaced. Raj Kumar Mishra, additional SP, Noida STF, said further investigation is underway to identify Durrani’s associates and trace the wider network behind the recent murders.(With inputs from Advitya Bahl in Noida and Rahul Singh in Bulandshahr)
Article Summary: Naseem Durrani was wanted in connection with the Nov 16 murder of Sameer, who was shot around 20 times in an attack suspected to have stemmed from an ongoing gang rivalry. He was tracked during the early hours near Sikandra bypass. CCTV footage from the area showed him riding a scooter and repeatedly looking back at the pursuing police personnel.

Article Title: Fire station at Andheri may finally take shape
Article Text:
The proposed fire station site in Andheri





MUMBAI: A Nov 19 meeting chaired by revenue minister Chandrashekhar Bawankule is likely to pave the way for transferring a 5,513-sq-metre fire station plot on Veera Desai Road, Andheri, to the state govt.On Friday, BJP corporator Rupesh Sawarkar met BMC commissioner Ashwini Bhide, seeking completion of the land transfer and construction tender process within 90 days. Article Title: HC suspends gangster Mehandi's life term in Shaikh Naser murder case
Article Text:
Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court on Thursday suspended the life sentence of gangster Shaikh Imran Mehandi alias Dilawar in the 2011 murder of Shaikh Naser Shaikh Chand during the pendency of his appeal, citing that convicting a person merely on recovery of a knife was “dangerous”.This is the third murder case, apart from the Salim Qureshi and Sirajuddin Ansari murder cases, in which Mehandi has secured bail. He is unlikely to walk out of jail soon, though. His bail applications and pleas for suspension of sentence are pending in at least two more murder cases.A division bench of Justice Sandipkumar More and Justice Vaishali Patil-Jadhav directed Mehandi’s release on a PR bond of Rs25,000 with one surety of the same amount, “if not required in any other case”.A special MCOCA court on Aug 1, 2018, convicted Mehandi and accused number 5 Syed Jahir alias Shera Bakhar Qureshi of murdering Shaikh Naser. It sentenced them to life imprisonment, while acquitting five others. Mehandi’s appeal is pending before the high court.According to the prosecution, Naser was killed on Sept 9, 2011, through sedative-laced juice, strangulation and knife blows, and his body was buried at Irfan Farm House in Savangi.The FIR was lodged at Begumpura police station in March 2012.Mehandi’s counsel, advocate Rupesh Jaiswal, argued there was no direct or last-seen evidence and that Mehandi’s name surfaced only after Jahir’s disclosure statement, with the conviction resting solely on a knife recovery.The division bench of the high court noted that Naser’s body was exhumed seven months after burial and that the knife was recovered from an open place accessible to all. Convicting a person merely on its recovery was “dangerous”, it said, and the prosecution had to establish a complete chain of circumstances.The court accepted that “there is no presumption of innocence of the accused at the stage of post-conviction” and suspension in Section 302 cases “is an exception and not the rule”. But it said “in the instant case, considering that conviction of the applicant is based only on recovery of the knife at his instance, there is a good scope for him to succeed in the appeal”. The appeal, recently filed, was unlikely to be heard soon, the high court said.The court ordered that the life sentence imposed on Aug 1, 2018, “is hereby suspended during the pendency of this appeal”. It clarified that its observations would not affect the merits of the appeal.On Sept 15, Supreme Court had suspended Mehandi’s life sentence in the 2012 murder of former corporator Salim Qureshi. Besides the pending bail pleas in at least two more murder cases, he faces trials in Nilesh Mhatre, Sindubai Mhatre and Sirajuddin murder cases, all registered in 2012.
Article Summary: Aurangabad bench of Bombay high court suspends the life sentence of gangster Shaikh Imran Mehandi alias Dilawar in the 2011 murder of Shaikh Naser Shaikh Chand. A division bench of Justice Sandipkumar More and Justice Vaishali Patil- Jadhav directed Me handi’s release on a PR bond of Rs25,000 with one surety.

Article Title: Sarpanch’s son drowns in Padmavati dam after fixing village water pipeline
Article Text:
The victim’s body was recovered from the dam with the assistance of a National Disaster Response Force team

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar:





A 25-year-old man, son of the sarpanch of Masrul village in Buldhana district, drowned in Padmavati dam in Bhokardan taluka of Jalna district while swimming back to the shore after completing work on the village water supply pipeline on Thursday.The deceased was identified as Madhukar Mahale. Paradh police of Jalna district registered a case of accidental death.Madhukar is survived by his mother, wife, two daughters and a son. His father, Shakuntalabai Mahale, is the sarpanch of Masrul village on the border of Buldhana and Jalna districts.Padmavati dam is on the border of the two districts. It had been the source of water for several neighbouring villages in both the districts, said Jalna superintendent of police Teghbir Singh Sandhu.The water from this dam has a pipeline connected to a well that caters to Masrul villagers. The water pump and the pipeline had developed a snag. The victim, Madhukar, along with a gram panchayat member, went to the dam and swam their way to the water pump.Paradh’s assistant inspector Sachin Khamgal, citing the eyewitnesses’ statement, said Madhukar had gone to the dam around 2.30pm with the gram panchayat member, K K Sinkar, to connect the pipeline to a public well in the dam’s submerged area.The well is part of the water supply scheme through which Padmavati dam water reaches Masrul village.After completing the work, the two attempted to swim back to the shore. Madhukar was exhausted midway and drowned. Sinkar managed to reach the shore and alerted villagers, following which a search and rescue operation was launched.Disaster management officer Sambhaji Pawar reached the spot with a rescue team. After an intensive search lasting around three hours, Madhukar’s body was recovered from the dam with the assistance of a National Disaster Response Force team.His body was taken to a Dhad-based state medical facility late on Thursday. An autopsy was performed on Friday morning before the body was handed over to Madhukar’s family members. His last rites were performed in the afternoon.Madhukar was known for taking an active role in addressing villagers’ problems. His death while working on the village’s water supply project plunged Masrul into mourning, said Balu Patil, a resident of the village.
Article Summary: The deceased was identified as Madhukar Mahale. He is the son of the sarpanch of Masrul village in Buldhana district. The water pump and the pipeline had developed a snag. The victim and a gram panchayat member went to the dam and swam their way to the water pump. After completing the work, the two attempted to swim back to the shore.
